{{short description|French bio-mathematician (born 1953)}}
'''Pierre Auger''' (born March 8, 1953) is a French [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|bio-mathematician]] and a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]]<ref name="liste">{{cite web|title=Liste des membres de l'Académie des sciences|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-A/pierre-auger.html|website=academie-sciences.fr|date=}}</ref>  and Director of Exceptional Class Research at the [[Research Institute for Development, Communication and School Partnership|Research Institute for Development]].<ref>{{cite web|title=IRD|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Pierre_Auger2|date=}}</ref> Pierre Auger's research field concerns the [[mathematical modelling]] of biological systems.

== Education and career ==
Auger was born in [[Neuilly-sur-Seine]] and studied at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University of Paris 6]] (1973-1977), where he obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[Nuclear physics|Nuclear Physics]] at the [[Institut de physique nucléaire d'Orsay|Institut de Physique Nucléaire]] d'Orsay in 1979 and his Doctorate in Physics. "Mathematical models of hierarchical systems" at the [[University of Angers]] in 1982. He was admitted to the CAPES in [[Physical Sciences]] in 1983, and became a certified Professor of Physics and Chemistry at the Lycée Technique Pasteur in [[Hénin-Beaumont]], Pas de Calais from 1984 to 1986 and then a certified Professor in Metallurgy at the Lycée Diderot in [[Paris]] from 1986 to 1987. He continued his career as a lecturer at the Biophysics Laboratory of the Faculty of Pharmacy of Dijon from 1987 to 1990, and Professor of Universities at the Ecology Laboratory of the [[University of Burgundy]] in [[Dijon]] from 1990 to 1992 and then Professor at the [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1|Claude Bernard University]] in [[Lyon]] from 1993 to 2004. He has been a research director at IRD since 2004. He was elected correspondent (1999) and then member of the French Academy of sciences (2003) in the Integrative Biology section.<ref name="liste" />

== Scientific work ==
Pierre Auger is a specialist in mathematical modelling in [[ecology]] and [[environmental science]]s.<ref>J.D. Murray, Mathematical Biology, Berlin, Heidelberg, Springer-Verlag, 1989</ref><ref name=":0">P. Auger, C. Lett et J.-C. Poggiale, Modélisation mathématique en écologie : cours et exercices corrigés. Mathématiques appliquées pour le Master/SMAI, Dunod: Sciences sup Série en co-édition avec les Editions de l’IRD, 2010, 302 <abbr>p.</abbr></ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Exercices corrigés|url=https://www.dunod.com/sciences-techniques/modelisation-mathematique-en-ecologie-cours-et-exercices-corriges|date=}}</ref> He has contributed to the development of "variable aggregation methods", the aim of which is to build from a detailed or "complete" model, a reduced model governing only a few global variables in the long term.<ref>P. Auger, Hierarchically organized systems: Dynamics and Thermodynamics. Applications to Physics, Biology and Economics, Pergamon Press, 1989, 210 <abbr>p.</abbr></ref> In the 1990s, with the mathematicians Robert Roussarie and Jean-Christophe Poggiale of the University of Dijon, he formalized the method as part of the centre variety theorem (2010-2014).<ref>Contribution Française à la Conférence de Rio, Juin 1992, UNESCO, SCOPE-FRANCE, (Scientific Committee On the Problems of the Environnement), Pierre Auger, Jacques Baudry et Frédéric Fournier éditeurs., Hiérarchie et Echelles en Ecologie, Naturalia publications, 1992</ref><ref>P. Auger, R. Bravo de la Parra, J.C. Poggiale, E. Sánchez, T. Nguyen Huu, Aggregation of variables and applications to population dynamics. In: P. Magal, S. Ruan (Eds.), Structured Population Models in Biology and Epidemiology, Lecture Notes in Mathematics, Mathematical Biosciences Subseries, Berlin, Springer, 2008, vol. 1936, <abbr>p.</abbr> 209-263</ref><ref>P. Auger, R. Bravo de la Parra, J.C. Poggiale, E. Sanchez, L. Sanz, « Aggregation methods in dynamical systems variables and applications in population and community dynamics », ''Physics of Life Reviews'', 2008, 5</ref>

Pierre Auger has been particularly interested with his collaborators in the applications of variable aggregation methods to the emergence of global behaviors in complex multi-scale systems. At IRD, he contributed to the modelling of population dynamics of large herbivore populations at Amboseli Natural Park in [[Kenya]] with the ACC ([[African Conservation Centre|African Conservation Center]]) (2010-2014).<ref>Nyaliki Mose V., et al., « Modeling herbivore population dynamics in the Amboseli National Park, Kenya : Application of spatial aggregation of variables to derive a master model », ''Ecological Complexity'', octobre 2012, <abbr>p.</abbr> 42-51</ref>

This study highlighted the need to maintain corridors between Amboseli and other parks and ecosystems in Kenya and [[Tanzania]] in order to maintain biodiversity and avoid the extinction of certain species. During his expatriation stays as an IRD researcher in [[Morocco]] (2008-2012) and [[Senegal]] (2012-2017), Pierre Auger contributed to the development of new mathematical models combining ecological and economic dynamics. In particular, it proposed bio-economic models of fisheries with a variable price of the resource on the market depending on supply and demand.<ref>Clark, C., Mathematical bioeconomics: the optimal management of renewable resources, New York, Wiley-Interscience, 1976</ref><ref>Auger P., Lett C. (2018), [https://www.encyclopedie-environnement.org/vivant/modeles-mathematiques-peche/ Les modèles mathématiques peuvent aider à mieux gérer la pêche, Encyclopédie de l’Environnement], {{ISSN|2555-0950}}.</ref> These models have been successfully used to explain observed trends in catches, fishing effort and market price of a species of the grouper family, commonly known as "thiof", in overfishing<ref>Cury, P., Miserey, Y., Une mer sans poissons, Calmann-Lévy, 2008</ref><ref>Thiao, D., Chaboud, C., Samba, A., Laloé, F., Cury, P., « Economic dimension of the collapse of the ‘false cod ‘ Epinephelus aeneus in a context of ineffective management of the small-scale fisheries in Senegal. », ''Journal of Marine Science'', 2012, 34(3), <abbr>p.</abbr> 305–311</ref> situation in Senegal, in collaboration with the Centre Océanographique de [[Dakar]]-Thiaroye (CRODT).<ref>Brochier T., et al., « Can overexploited fisheries recover by self-organization? Reallocation of fishing effort as an emergent governance. », ''Marine Policy (JMPO)'', 2018, 95, <abbr>p.</abbr> 46-56</ref>

== Educational activities ==
At the Claude Bernard University in Lyon, Pierre Auger contributed to the creation of an original Biomathematics course for the part concerning the mathematical modelling of biological systems (1993-2004).  He is co-author of a book on mathematical modelling in ecology.<ref name=":0" /> He has been co-supervisor of many thesis students in Africa and Vietnam, particularly since his recruitment at IRD.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thèse modélisation mathématique|url=https://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/tel-00633827/document|date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Thèses (2)|url=http://horizon.documentation.ird.fr/exl-doc/pleins_textes/divers09-08/010035320.pdf|date=}}</ref>

== Other Institutional Responsibilities ==
Source:<ref>{{cite web|title=CV|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/AugerP_bio032011.pdf|website=academie-sciences.fr|date=}}</ref>
* Head of the "Mathematical Biology" research team in the UMR [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] 5558 at Claude Bernard Lyon 1 University, (1993-2004).
* President of CSS3: "Sciences of Ecological Systems" of the IRD (2003-2007).
* Director of the Research Unit 079 IRD GEODES (2005-2008).
* Member of the ANR Steering Committee "Complex Systems" (2008-2010).
* Director of the International Joint Unit (UMI) 209 of the IRD, the Mathematical and Computer Modelling Unit of Complex Systems (UMMISCO), UMI under the supervision of [[Sorbonne University]] in France, Cadi Ayyad University in Morocco, Cheikh-Anta-Diop University and [[Gaston Berger University|Gaston-Berger University]] in Senegal, [[University of Yaoundé|Yaoundé University 1]] in [[Cameroon]] and [[Hanoi University of Science and Technology|Hanoi University]] of Science and Technology in [[Vietnam]] (2009-2013).
* President of the Committee of Developing Countries (COPED) of the Academy of Sciences (2017-...).<ref>{{cite web|title=COPED|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Codeveloppement/coped.html|website=academie-sciences.fr|date=}}</ref>
